The parametrised test at :369-403 asserts success only. A removal moved before the commit in rename, copy or upload would not be caught by the tests read. The mutation was predicted, not run.

The line references hold: thumbnail_migration.py:85, 93, 101, 114, 119, 122 and 125. No test in backend/tests calls migrate_thumbnail_slots directly or reads its return value. slow_migrate at test_thumbnail_slots.py:935-939 passes the value on without asserting it. The caplog tests at :992-998, :1018-1024 and :1039-1043 count messages containing the path, at WARNING level, so the INFO summary line is never checked. thumbnail_migration.py:28 catches NotADirectoryError. No file in backend/tests mentions NotADirectory. test_absent_file_* at test_thumbnail_slots.py:786-807 leave the parent directory missing, which raises FileNotFoundError. Without this arm the error falls to :30-31, returns unknown and keeps the pointer with a warning at every startup, instead of emptying or repointing it, so the claim about what it decides holds. The prediction was not run.

upload.py:360-363 is the branch, and spec section 2 states the case. test_upload.py's only commit matches are the seeding calls at :416 and :429. The session-commit replacements in backend/tests are test_trash_purge_loop.py:479 and :513, test_markdown_image_import.py:694 and test_thumbnail_slots.py:912, and none goes through complete_upload. The upload tests at test_thumbnail_slots.py:177, :222-264 and :455 all reach a successful commit.

thumbnail_migration.py:32-33 and :82-87 behave as claimed, and scanner.py:161-164 with :501 skips the row. Spec section 3's states and section 2's failure list do not contain this outcome, and invariants.md has an empty Revisions section. The group key ('unknown', rel) can hold several rows, which contradicts section 3's 'names its own file alone'. Qualification: 'no way out' means no way inside the app. Purge also fails, because fileops.py:640-641 calls unlink on the directory. Removing the directory by hand makes the next startup treat the row as absent. A stat error recovers by itself at the next startup (test_thumbnail_slots.py:1026-1029). I found no ordinary way to get a directory at a pointer's path, since the pointer's own cache file would occupy it.

upload.py:278-280 flushes a DELETE, and generation runs at :290 before the commit at :359. A copy of the pre-change code in the main checkout, whose commit is not confirmed as origin/develop, generates at lines 257-272 before the lookup. database.py:15-27 and config.py:10 set no timeout, and no busy_timeout is set in database.py or config.py. Generators have subprocess timeouts of 30 to 60 seconds (thumbnail.py:32, :62, :126, :206, :463), which bounds the hold. Reach is narrow: init_upload answers 409 while the trashed file is still on disk (decisions.md item 7), so this needs a trashed row whose file has already gone. The 5-second sqlite3 default and the behaviour under contention were not exercised.

The touch points do not list physical_delete. Comparing the main checkout's fileops.py:119-126 with thumbnail.py:624-631 shows the same walk and stop on OSError, so behaviour is unchanged by reading.

thumbnail_migration.py:83-84 discards the id and logs only the path. Spec section 8 requires each failed row's warning to name the row and the path, and :111-113 does name both. The tests at test_thumbnail_slots.py:1024 and :1043 check only the path, so they would not catch this.

specification_compliance: All 13 listed findings match the code at the checked-out tree, with the qualifications in their notes.
I13: the code removes the ghost's picture after the commit in copy, rename, move and upload. Only the move failure half is tested.
Spec section 8's warning that names the row and the path is met for os.replace failures (thumbnail_migration.py:111-113), not for the unknown state (:83-84).
The unknown migration state has no support in the spec or in a recorded revision.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Migration keeps the pointer for a stat error or a non-regular file (thumbnail_migration.py:30-33, :82-87). r1 sent this question to a human, and no decision is recorded.
Purging a row whose pointer names a directory raises at fileops.py:641, because unlink is called on a directory, and the migration now keeps such pointers. No ordinary way to reach this was found.

An upload over a reused row whose commit fails leaves the slot already rewritten, since upload.py:361 removes the new slot only when there is no reused row. The spec states only the new-id case. The target file also stays on disk, so a later scan would match the picture for a .by-id row.
regression_risks: Upload's ghost and new-slot failure branch can change without a test failing (TEST-4, R2-TEST-1).
The migration summary counts can drift without a test failing (R2-TEST-2).
Removing or weakening the scan's path-form guard would not fail the I16 test (TEST-3).
Other writers can wait on the SQLite write lock during generation when an upload replaces a trashed ghost (CONC-1).
test_coverage: Read test_thumbnail_slots.py's ghost, scan-branch and migration sections and the conftest client fixture. conftest.py:134-140 stubs the startup scan, so lifespan restarts in these tests never exercise the scan's guard.

Missing tests confirmed by search and reading: I13 failure for rename, copy and upload; upload commit failure; migration counts; NotADirectoryError; and a path-form row whose file is absent, or that has a transparent source or letterboxed dimensions, in a scan.
